title: Провокация Ильи в раздевалке  (Ilya's Provocation in the Locker Room)

segments.t: Alone with Max in the staff locker room, Ilya smugly taunts him about Sasha and warns that nobody will believe a word Max says. Before Max can react, Ilya slams his own face against a metal locker door and collapses to the floor just as the others rush in.
Ты че, совсем жива сошел, что ли?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'I will go close the door.' Notice how Russian expresses 'go' and 'to close' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Sasha answers right away.
'So, did you get a good night's sleep?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'got enough sleep' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'What is the matter, Sasha will not let you near her?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'they give' without extra filler words.
'What did you just say?' Sasha addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to say'. Max answers right away.
'Who is going to believe you?' Max brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'who' in a few short words.
'Lavrov, what on earth are you doing?' Sasha anchors the line on 'Lavrov', while 'are doing' completes the thought.
Ты че, совсем жива сошел, что ли?
'Have you completely lost your mind or what?' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'stepped off' places the action in the masculine past tense. Sasha answers right away.
'Stop it, what are you doing?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'enough' and finishing on 'are you doing'.
'Come on, get up.' Notice how Russian expresses 'what' and 'get up' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Enough already, what are you doing.' Sasha anchors the line on 'enough', while 'are doing' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
'I did not even lay a finger on him!' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'him' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Well, actually, that is exactly what happened.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'there was'.
'Let go of me.' The grammar packs 'let go' and 'me' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Ты че, совсем жива сошел, что ли?
That wraps up this scene as in the locker room, Ilya taunts Max about Sasha and then deliberately slams his own face into a locker so the staff will think Max beat him up. See you next time!
